intro: The twenty-two letters of the Hebrew alphabet as read by the mystical tradition: each letter is a picture, a number, a sound and a gate. Block (square) script is the printed form; cursive is the handwritten form used in modern Israel. Classification into Mothers, Doubles and Simples follows the Sefer Yetzirah; the Tarot and planetary keys follow the Golden Dawn attribution, which differs from the Sefer Yetzirah's own planetary order (given separately).

aleph.name: Aleph
aleph.meaning: Strength, leader, the first; the ox that pulls the plough and the breath before any sound is made.
aleph.spiritual: Aleph is silent: it is the unspoken source from which every other letter emerges, the One that precedes the many. Its form is two Yods joined by a diagonal Vav, the upper and lower waters held together by a line of connection, which the mystics read as heaven and earth united in the human being. As the first letter of Elohim and of Adam it stands for the unity behind creation and for the paradox that the mightiest power is the quietest.

bet.name: Bet
bet.meaning: House, dwelling, family, the inside; what is contained and what contains.
bet.spiritual: Bet is the first letter of the Torah (Bereshit, In the beginning), and the sages ask why creation begins with the second letter rather than the first: because Bet is a house open on one side, closed above, below and behind, so that the created world looks forward and does not pry into what lies before, above or beneath it. Bet is the blessing (berakhah) and the home in which the divine chooses to dwell. As a double letter it carries two sounds, the hard B of form and the soft V of breath.
bet.words: Bereshit (in the beginning), berakhah (blessing), bayit (house), ben (son), binah (understanding)

gimel.name: Gimel
gimel.meaning: Camel, to carry, to lift up, to deal generously; movement toward another.
gimel.spiritual: The Talmud pictures Gimel as a rich man running after Dalet, the poor man, to give him charity, which is why Gimel's foot is extended toward the letter that follows it. Gimel is gemilut chasadim, the bestowal of loving-kindness, and the camel that carries provisions across the desert. It is also the number three, the reconciling third that joins any two opposites, and the bridge between the house of Bet and the door of Dalet.
gimel.words: gamal (camel), gadol (great), gemilut chasadim (acts of kindness), ga'al (to redeem)

dalet.name: Dalet
dalet.meaning: Door, threshold, path, the way in; also the poor one who is bent at the doorway.
dalet.spiritual: Dalet is the door of the house of Bet and the poor person (dal) who receives what Gimel brings: humility, the lowered head, the doorway that must be stooped through. Its shape is a lintel and a doorpost, and the tradition reads it as the four directions and the four worlds through which the soul descends and returns. Dalet is the choice at the threshold: to open or to stay closed.

he.name: He
he.pictograph: window, person with raised arms, breath
he.meaning: Behold, breath, revelation, a window; to show and to be shown.
he.spiritual: He is the letter of breath and of the divine name: it appears twice in YHVH and is the letter added to Abram and Sarai when they became Abraham and Sarah, the breath of the higher life joined to the human name. Its form is a Dalet with a small detached Yod inside: the door with a point of light within it, the opening through which the hidden shows itself. The sages say this world was created with He, because it is open below for anyone to fall out and open above for anyone to return.
he.words: hineh (behold), ha- (the), hallel (praise), YHVH (the Name), Hevel (breath, Abel)

vav.name: Vav
vav.meaning: Nail, hook, and; that which joins, fixes and connects one thing to another.
vav.spiritual: Vav is the conjunction 'and', the letter that joins heaven to earth and clause to clause, and its straight vertical form is the line of descent, the pillar, the spine. As the sixth letter it is the six days of creation and the six directions of space held on one axis. Vav is the third letter of the divine name and stands for the connecting principle that lets the upper flow into the lower; the tradition calls it the hook on which the whole tent of the world hangs.
vav.words: vav (hook), ve- (and), the six days, the pillar of the spine

zayin.name: Zayin
zayin.meaning: Weapon, sword, plough; to cut, to divide, and by dividing to nourish (zan, to feed).
zayin.spiritual: Zayin is a crowned Vav, a Vav with a crown upon its head, and the crown is the Sabbath: the seventh day that completes the six of Vav. It is the sword that cuts and the plough that breaks the earth so that food can grow, so the same letter begins zayin (weapon) and mazon (sustenance): struggle and nourishment are one root. Zayin is the letter of memory (zakhor, remember) and of the seed (zera) that carries the past into the future.

chet.name: Chet
chet.pictograph: fence, wall, inner chamber, tent wall
chet.meaning: Fence, enclosure, private room; to protect, to separate, to hold life within.
chet.spiritual: Chet is the first letter of chai (life) and chesed (loving-kindness), and its form is two Vavs joined by a thin roof, a doorway that is also a chuppah, the wedding canopy under which two become one. It is the fence that keeps life safe and the inner chamber of the heart; as the number eight it stands one beyond the seven of nature, the new beginning above the natural cycle, which is why circumcision and the covenant fall on the eighth day. Chet is also the letter of sin (chet) when the fence becomes a wall that shuts life out.
chet.words: chai (life), chesed (kindness), chokhmah (wisdom), chuppah (canopy), chalom (dream), chet (sin)

tet.name: Tet
tet.meaning: Basket, container, coiled serpent; good that is hidden within, to surround and enclose.
tet.spiritual: Tet is the first letter of tov (good) and its shape curls inward like a serpent biting its tail or a vessel holding something precious: hidden goodness, the good that must be drawn out from concealment. It is the ninth letter, the nine months of gestation, the womb in which what is good is formed in secret. The serpent of Tet can be the coiled power of the lower nature or, turned upward, the wisdom that heals, and the tradition says that when Tet first appeared in the Torah it was in the words 'and God saw that it was good'.

yod.name: Yod
yod.meaning: Hand, work, deed; the point, the seed, the smallest beginning from which all unfolds.
yod.spiritual: Yod is the smallest letter, a single point suspended in the air, and yet every other letter begins with it: the scribe's pen touches the parchment as a Yod before any stroke is drawn. It is the first letter of the divine name and of Israel, the spark of will before it extends into form, the hand of God at work. As ten it is the completion of the units and the return to one on a higher level, the ten utterances of creation and the ten sefirot. The sages say the world to come was created with Yod, because it is a world of pure point without extension.
yod.words: yad (hand), YHVH (the Name), Yisrael (Israel), yom (day), yesod (foundation)

kaf.name: Kaf
kaf.pictograph: open palm, bent hand, cupped hand
kaf.meaning: Palm of the hand, to cover, to bend, to allow; capacity, and 'like' or 'as' (the prefix of comparison).
kaf.spiritual: Kaf is the open palm that holds and the crown (keter) that rests on the head; its curved form is the hand bent to receive and to give. As the prefix ke- it means 'like', the letter of resemblance, by which one thing is understood through another. Kaf is the first letter of kavanah, the directed intention of the heart, and of kavod, the glory that fills the vessel. Its final form drops straight down below the line, the open hand reaching into the depths.

lamed.name: Lamed
lamed.meaning: Goad, staff, to teach and to learn, to urge forward; toward (the prefix le-).
lamed.spiritual: Lamed is the only letter that rises above the line, a tower reaching upward: the tradition calls it the king of the letters and pictures it as a heart (lev) aspiring toward heaven, since Lamed is the first letter of lev and of limud, learning. The goad that drives the ox becomes the staff of the teacher and the pull of longing that moves the student. Lamed stands at the centre of the alphabet; with the Kaf before it and the Mem after it, it spells melekh, king, in reverse: the crown, the heart and the water of wisdom.
lamed.words: lev (heart), lamad (to learn), Torah is limud, le- (to, toward), lashon (tongue)

mem.name: Mem
mem.meaning: Water, the womb, the mother; the flowing source and what comes forth from it.
mem.spiritual: Mem is the mother letter of water and of the womb, mayim, the fluid source out of which forms condense. It has two shapes: the open Mem, water that flows and reveals, and the closed final Mem, a sealed square that holds the hidden waters of the world to come. Mem is forty: the forty days of the flood, the forty years in the wilderness, the forty weeks of gestation, the measure of a full transformation. It begins the words for king (melekh), wisdom's mother Torah (Moshe received it), and the Messiah, and it sits at the centre of emet, truth.
mem.words: mayim (water), Moshe (Moses), melekh (king), mashiach (anointed), mikveh (immersion pool)

nun.name: Nun
nun.meaning: Fish, seed, to propagate, continuity of life through generations; faithfulness.
nun.spiritual: Nun is the fish swimming in the waters of Mem and the seed that carries life from one generation to the next; the Aramaic nun means fish, and the tradition reads the letter as faithfulness (ne'eman) and as the fall and rise of the soul, since the bent Nun bows and the final Nun stands straight. Fifty is the fiftieth gate of understanding and the jubilee year when everything returns to its source. Nun begins the words for soul (nefesh, neshamah), prophet (navi) and miracle (nes).
nun.words: nefesh, neshamah (soul), navi (prophet), nes (miracle), ner (lamp), ne'eman (faithful)

samekh.name: Samekh
samekh.meaning: Support, to lean upon, to uphold; a circle of protection.
samekh.spiritual: Samekh is a closed circle, the only letter with no opening, and the tradition reads it as the divine support that surrounds the one who falls (somekh noflim, upholder of the fallen). It is the ring, the wedding band, the cycle of the year, the wheel that turns without beginning or end; its value sixty is the number of the mighty men around Solomon's bed and the measure of the seconds and minutes by which time is upheld. Samekh is the hidden order that carries what cannot carry itself.
samekh.words: samakh (to support), sod (secret), sefer (book), sukkah (shelter), seder (order)

ayin.name: Ayin
ayin.meaning: Eye, to see, to know by seeing; a spring or fountain; appearance.
ayin.spiritual: Ayin is the eye and, like Aleph, it is silent: it is the seeing that happens without sound, the inner eye and the outer eye joined in one glyph, two branches on one stem. Seventy is the seventy nations, the seventy elders and the seventy faces of the Torah, the full range of what can be seen from different angles. Ayin is also the letter of the evil eye and of the good eye: sight can grasp and covet or it can bless. The letter begins olam (world), the concealment (he'elem) in which the infinite hides so that a world can be seen at all.
ayin.words: ayin (eye, spring), olam (world), anavah (humility), etz (tree), avodah (service)

pe.name: Pe
pe.meaning: Mouth, speech, edge, opening; to speak, to blow, to scatter.
pe.spiritual: Pe is the mouth, and inside its curve the white space forms a hidden Bet: the house within the mouth, the inner word before it is spoken. The scribes note that in the Torah's account of the tablets the letters were engraved 'through and through', and Pe is the letter of that speech which creates and also of the edge (peh) of the sword that divides. It is double, the hard P of the word that strikes and the soft F of the breath that whispers. Eighty is the age at which Moses began to speak for God.

tzadi.name: Tzadi
tzadi.pictograph: fish-hook, trail, to hunt, a person kneeling
tzadi.meaning: Hook, to hunt, to lie in wait; the righteous one (tzaddik), the side (tzad).
tzadi.spiritual: Tzadi is the letter of the tzaddik, the righteous person, and its form is a Nun bowed in humility with a Yod, the divine spark, joined to it: the soul that bends and the point of light it carries. The bent Tzadi is the righteous one in this world; the final Tzadi stands upright, the same soul in the world to come. It is the fish-hook that draws souls out of the water and the hunter's patience. Ninety is the age of Sarah when the promise was fulfilled, and the tradition counts thirty-six hidden tzaddikim on whom the world rests.
tzadi.words: tzaddik (righteous), tzedakah (charity, justice), tzel (shadow), tzelem (image), Tzion (Zion)

qof.name: Qof
qof.pictograph: back of the head, eye of a needle, horizon, monkey
qof.meaning: Back of the head, what lies behind; the eye of a needle; holiness (kodesh) and the cycle of time.
qof.spiritual: Qof is the letter that descends below the line, like the final letters but by nature, the tail of the monkey (qof) that imitates the human and the eye of the needle through which the camel of Gimel must pass. It stands for what is behind and beneath: the unconscious, the horizon, the sun's circuit (hekef) around the earth. Qof begins kodesh, holiness, and the opposite, the ape that mimics holiness; the tradition warns that the two look alike from the front and only differ in what lies behind. One hundred is the full measure, the return of the ten to its own tenfold power.

resh.name: Resh
resh.meaning: Head, chief, beginning; the face that turns, poverty when the head is bowed (rash).
resh.spiritual: Resh is the head and the beginning (reshit) and the face that turns either toward or away. It is a Dalet without its corner, the door with its edge rounded, and the tradition contrasts the two: Dalet bends to receive, Resh is the head that can be lifted in leadership or in pride, the wicked (rasha) or the head of the year (Rosh Hashanah). It is two hundred, the letter of Mercury in the Sefer Yetzirah and of the Sun in the Golden Dawn, the mind that governs and the light that reveals.
resh.words: rosh (head), reshit (beginning), ruach (spirit, wind), rachamim (compassion), ra'ah (to see)

shin.name: Shin
shin.meaning: Tooth, to consume, to press, to change; fire that transforms; the Name (Shaddai).
shin.spiritual: Shin is the mother letter of fire, three flames rising from one root, the teeth that grind and the fire that consumes and transforms. It is the letter written on the mezuzah and on the tefillin for the name Shaddai and it stands for shalom, peace, the wholeness that fire refines. The right-pointed Shin and left-pointed Sin are one letter with two sounds, the fire that destroys and the fire that warms. Three hundred is the strength of Gideon's chosen men; the tradition says the letter of the world to come is a four-headed Shin whose fourth flame is not yet lit.
shin.words: shalom (peace), Shaddai (Almighty), shamayim (heavens), shem (name), Shabbat, shir (song)

tav.name: Tav
tav.meaning: Mark, sign, seal, covenant; the end, completion, truth's final letter.
tav.spiritual: Tav is the last letter and the seal: the ancient form was a simple cross, the mark set on the foreheads of the righteous in Ezekiel's vision and the signature at the end of a document. It closes the word emet, truth, whose letters are the first, the middle and the last of the alphabet, so that truth spans the whole. Tav is the completed world, the four hundred years of exile and the return, the Torah (which begins with Tav) and repentance (teshuvah), the turning back that completes the journey. Its form is a Dalet joined to a Nun: the door and the faithful soul that has passed through it.
tav.words: Torah, teshuvah (return), tefillah (prayer), tikkun (repair), tamim (whole), emet ends with Tav
